text:
ashley_acme: Hey team — our app hitting Redwood private endpoint through corp proxy is throwing TLS handshake failures since this morning. curl just gives `SSL: WRONG_VERSION_NUMBER` and requests intermittently 502. Anyone seen this with enterprise proxies?

sara: Sorry you're hitting this, Ashley. Can you paste a short `curl -v` output and the target hostname? Also are you using an explicit corporate TLS-inspecting proxy (MITM) or a pass-through LB? :eyes: 

ashley_acme: It's a corporate forward proxy that does TLS interception (they re-encrypt). Host: private.redwood-acme.example.com. Quick curl: 
```
$ curl -v https://private.redwood-acme.example.com/api/v1/health
* Connected to proxy.corp.local (10.0.0.5) port 8080 (#0)
* ALPN, offering http/1.1
* TLSv1.2 (INTERNAL), TLS unknown, Cipher is ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256
* SSL connection using TLSv1.2 / ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256
> GET /api/v1/health HTTP/1.1
> Host: private.redwood-acme.example.com
> User-Agent: curl/7.68.0
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
* Received HTTP/0.9 when not allowed
* Closing connection 0
curl: (55) Received HTTP/0.9 when not allowed
```

mike: Thanks. That `TLS: WRONG_VERSION_NUMBER` usually shows up when something speaking plain HTTP answers a TLS client, or when TLS versions/ciphers are incompatible. Because your proxy terminates and re-encrypts, we should check three legs: client->proxy, proxy->redwood, and redwood->(backend).

sara: Can you run these and paste outputs (mask secrets):
1) `openssl s_client -connect private.redwood-acme.example.com:443 -servername private.redwood-acme.example.com -alpn h2,http/1.1 -tls1_3`
2) `openssl s_client -connect proxy.corp.local:443 -servername private.redwood-acme.example.com -tls1_2`
3) `curl -v --proxy proxy.corp.local:8080 https://private.redwood-acme.example.com`

ashley_acme: Ran 2) against the proxy (they only expose 8080 for proxying so used -connect proxy.corp.local:8080):
```
$ openssl s_client -connect proxy.corp.local:8080 -servername private.redwood-acme.example.com -tls1_2
CONNECTED(00000003)
140086...: SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert protocol version
139...:errno=0
---
no peer certificate available
---
SSL handshake has read 7 bytes and written 126 bytes
---
```
Seems the proxy is actively negotiating to an older profile and sending an alert.

mike: That `tlsv1 alert protocol version` from the proxy suggests it's trying to limit to a lower version or the server (our side) is dropping the connection. On our end, can we see the nginx/ALB TLS config? Sara, do we have the config for that private host (which private deployment: VPC or dedicated?)

sara: Ashley, you're on Redwood Private VPC (customer-managed control plane). I pulled the deployment: private.redwood-acme.example.com is fronted by a HA nginx pool with `ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3; ssl_ciphers 'ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256GCM: ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256: ...'` and `ssl_prefer_server_ciphers on`.

mike: Two likely mismatches: (1) proxy is doing TLS inspection and presenting a client cert or cipher list we don't accept, (2) proxy might strip SNI or use a different SNI value so the server picks the wrong cert (or TLS profile). Please ask the proxy team to confirm they forward SNI and not downgrade ALPN to `http/1.0` or strip `h2`.

ashley_acme: Confirmed proxy team says they inject their own cert and re-encrypt to backend with a fixed cipher profile that does not include some ECDHE-only ciphers. They listed allowed ciphers: `RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384` and TLS 1.2 only.

mike: Ok — our server currently prefers ECDHE ciphers and was compiled with ECDSA/ECDHE priorities. If the proxy only advertises RSA-only ciphers, we might not match if server requires ECDHE or if `ssl_ecdh_curve` is strict. Two remediation paths:
- Short term (fast): Add RSA-based TLS ciphers to the server cipher list to accept proxy's re-encryption profile. Example: `ssl_ciphers 'ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384:RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384';` and reload.
- Better: Ask proxy to enable ECDHE ciphers and TLS1.2+ and ensure SNI/ALPN passthrough or configure their re-encrypt profile to include ECDHE-RSA ciphers.

sara: Also request from proxy team: a `tcpdump -w` capture of the handshake or an `openssl s_client -connect proxy.corp.local:8080 -servername private.redwood-acme.example.com -tls1_2 -msg` output so we can see the ClientHello/CipherList. Example commands we need them to run: 
```
# on proxy
openssl s_client -connect private.redwood-acme.example.com:443 -servername private.redwood-acme.example.com -tls1_2 -msg
# or capture
sudo tcpdump -s 0 -w /tmp/proxy_handshake.pcap host private.redwood-acme.example.com and port 443
```

ashley_acme: Proxy team attached a small excerpt of the ClientHello cipher list (sanitized): `CipherSuites: TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256`

mike: That looks ok but if the proxy terminates TLS for the client and then connects to the backend with only RSA ciphers, we need server to accept `TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256`. Our nginx build supports it but our config excluded RSA ciphers for security reasons. If you change the server cipher string to include the RSA-GCM entries it should restore compatibility.

ashley_acme: If we relax ciphers on the server, are there security implications? Proxy team insists they must do TLS inspection for DLP.

mike: Yes, accepting RSA ciphers is slightly weaker than ECDHE in forward secrecy terms (if using RSA key-exchange rather than ECDHE). But `TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256` uses RSA key exchange (no PFS). If you require PFS, ask proxy to reconfigure to use ECDHE re-encryption with their own ECDHE keys. If that's not possible, assess the risk: traffic into the proxy is still inspected; between proxy and server will be encrypted but without PFS. For many enterprise setups this is allowed.

ashley_acme: Trying the quick change now. Will update after reload.

eng-oncall-bot: Deploy started for config change on private-redwood-nginx-2a (rolling): 1/3 nodes updated.

ashley_acme: After adding `RSA-AES` entries and reloading, health checks pass and API calls succeed through the proxy again. Thanks all! :thumbsup:

sara: Great — leaving this thread open for 24h to monitor. If you want, we can schedule a follow-up to help the proxy team move to an ECDHE-compliant profile.

mike: Also adding a note to run periodic handshake compatibility tests from their proxy IPs as part of our private onboarding checklist.

ashley_acme: Appreciate it. Will coordinate with our security team to plan a long-term fix.
